writing.overall_comment: A solid, well-structured Python test-engineer persona with good conventions and examples, but it needs an explicit output contract, clearer scope boundaries/hand-back rules, and de-duplication of the repeated framework and skill lists.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description clearly signals test generation in Python with named frameworks and specialties, so a main agent can route on it, though it lacks sharper 'use when' triggers to distinguish it from a general python-development agent.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, naming rules, AAA structure, coverage expectations, and a 6-step workflow are explicit, but there is no concrete output contract (file paths, naming of test files, or deliverable format) and the prompt references an external README for templates.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: The 'should not' list gives some anti-patterns but never states hard limits such as not editing production code or when to hand back to a development/design agent.

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: Framework and tooling lists are duplicated across '核心技术' and '您的角色', and '集成技能' claims api-design and database-design skills not declared in the frontmatter, wasting tokens and creating inconsistency.

suggestions: In the boundaries/'should not' section, add hard limits that explicitly prohibit editing production code and specify the conditions for handing work back to a development or design agent.

In the prompt's output/deliverable instructions, replace the external README template reference with an inline template and define concrete file paths, test-file naming rules, and the required deliverable format.

In '核心技术', '您的角色', and '集成技能', remove duplicated framework/tooling lists and either declare the api-design and database-design skills in the frontmatter or remove them from the claimed integration skills.
